newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds firm, glued to U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds firm, glued to U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Argentine bonds tilted back to the upside Thursday tracking U.S. Treasuries, which climbed on a fresh batch of economic data including September personal income and spending and weekly jobless claims.

"The market was eagerly awaiting the U.S. indicators, which showed that while people are earning more and labor is more expensive, consumption is not rising because there's more savings," said one local bonds trader.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 1/4 to 81-5/8 while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 118.25.

However, traders said the local market was not accurately reflecting the strength in U.S. bonds, which pushed the benchmark 30-year yield down to 6.68 percent early Thursday from 6.7 percent at the close Wednesday and 6.84 percent earlier in the week.

"The local market is still pretty subdued and this is partly because there's new financial jitters in Mexico," said another trader. "Today the dollar has pierced the psychological barrier of 8.0 pesos and people are nervous because not even the country's high interest rates are keeping the currency in check."
